headline: Elected Mike O'Brien chair and John Baker vice chair; approved previous minutes; discussed Comprehensive Plan and Building Typologies Report.
summary: Members elected Mike O’Brien as chair and John Baker as vice chair. Members also approved the previous meeting minutes and discussed the Comprehensive Plan, the FY2027 work plan, and the Building Typologies Report, with no votes on those items.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting minutes, unanimously.
Elected Mike O’Brien as Chair, unanimously.
Elected John Baker as Vice Chair, unanimously.

Election of John Baker as Vice Chair
plain_text:
8/13/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Mike O’Brien, Chair; Brian Colombini; Matt Gile; John Baker; Ruby Tetrick; 
Trevor Thomas
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning
Guests Present: Thomas Renner, Mayor
Call to Order by: Mike
Meeting Start Time: 6:30 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Matt
Second: Ruby
Decision: Unanimous.
Motion carried
Discussion/Approval: Reorganization 
Motion by John, seconded by Matt, to elect Mike O’Brien as Chair of the Planning Commission. 
Voting: Unanimous. Motion carried.
Motion by Matt, seconded by Ruby, to elect John Baker as Vice Chair. Voting: Unanimous. 
Motion carried.
Discussion: Planning and Zoning Update 
Ravi gave a summary of the zoning permits issued during the 2026 fiscal year, as well as the 
permit applications the Development Review Board and Local Resources Advisory Board 
reviewed. Ravi gave an overview of the review process for permit applications involving historic 
buildings, and elements needed for buildings to qualify to be listed on the local historic register. 
Matt asked if the Planning Commission would be involved in discussions to add or remove new 
properties to the Local Historic Register. Ravi said that this process is still a work in progress, 
because the Local Resources Advisory Board is not tasked with soliciting property owners to list 
their properties on the register, but that the Planning Commission and City Council have a role in 
adding and removing properties on the local historic register. Thomas added that the intent of 
the Local Historic Register is to protect buildings that are intact and are significant landmarks 
within the City.
Ravi said that internal review processes for zoning permit applications have been refined earlier 
this year, which now involve Public Works earlier in the review process. Ravi said that this has 
extended review timelines to 6 to 8 weeks for zoning permit applications. Mike and John said 
that 6 to 8 weeks for permit review is good when compared to Act 250 or larger cities.
Ravi said that the Building Typologies Report is now complete, and that the Planning 
Commission can discuss this further at an upcoming meeting.
Ravi said that the commission will be involved in the drafting of the Comprehensive Plan in the 
coming months, and that he is aware that a larger overhaul of all of the City’s long-range plans 
will be needed eight years from now when the Comprehensive Plan is up for review again.
Ravi gave an updated on electric vehicle charging planning. John asked about statewide 
requirements for electric vehicle charging. Ravi said that the requirements are in the latest 
building energy standards, but not in the set of building energy standards currently in use, and 
that the commission could consider requiring electric vehicle charging instead of only 
incentivizing building the infrastructure.
Discussion: FY2027 Work Plan
Ravi gave an overview of the draft work plan, showing how it aligns with City Council’s Policies, 
Priorities and Strategies. Ravi said that he is working with Public Works to plan for future growth 
in the residential districts, and that the Building Typologies project helped with determining the 
feasibility of buildout on lots in the residential districts. Thomas spoke about prioritizing setting 
design parameters to make sure future development is in line with the City’s interests and 
character.
Matt asked if the City has any infrastructure constraints. Ravi said that he’s not aware of any 
infrastructure constraints based on the City’s current rate of growth, but that he is aware of 
potential long-term issues Public Works is worried about, like the placement of buildings behind 
buildings. Ravi said that the City will need to be mindful of which parts can accommodate more 
growth now, and which parts will need a longer timeframe to accommodate for growth based on 
current infrastructure.
Ravi said that the next Planning Commission meeting will include a longer discussion on the 
Comprehensive Plan, with deeper dives into particular sections in the coming months. Brian 
asked about coordination with other City boards, committees and departments on the 
development of the Comprehensive Plan. Ravi said that he has met with most boards and 
commissions multiple times to discuss goals and actions that pertain to them, and that there will 
be opportunities for the Planning Commission to reach out to them during the drafting of the 
Comprehensive Plan.
Discussion: Building Typologies Report – Introduction and Review
Ravi gave an overview of the Building Typologies project. Ravi said that the concept designs are 
based on typical lot sizes in the Residential B and Residential C Zoning Districts. Ravi said that 
the consultants concluded that the Residential A Zoning District would not be compatible for the 
project based on current densities and transit access. Matt asked about the financial feasibility 
to develop the concepts. Ravi said that that question was not in the scope of the study, as the 
consultants worked under the assumption that to build affordable, three-plus bedroom housing, 
external funding and tax credits would have to be involved. Ravi said that the project provides 
guidance to developers on the City’s interests.
City Updates
Updates from the Mayor
Thomas reviewed the recent election, the status of the hotel and housing project on 
Winooski Falls Way.
Updates from the Inclusion and Belonging Commission
Updates from City Staff
Ravi talked about the upcoming Comprehensive Plan Open House on August 27th
at the Senior Center from 5 pm to 7 pm, and the status of the Armory project.
Other Business
Adjourn
Motion by: John
Second: Brian
Meeting End Time: 7:53 pm
